newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto bull run fueling exchange listings boom.
newsitem.headline: Toronto bull run fueling exchange listings boom.

text.p: A bull run in Toronto stocks should prompt a slew of new listings from now until year-end, Ralph Shay, the Toronto Stock Exchange's vice-president of company listings and regulation, said Monday.
"If the current pace continues, we could have 30 or more," Shay said in an interview.

Canada's largest stock exchange listed 108 new companies in the first three quarters of 1996, against 56 in the same period a year earlier. However, the showing so far is nowhere near that of 1987, when the TSE listed 180 firms in the full year.
The TSE's key 300 Composite Index has risen 15.5 percent since the start of 1996, from 4,707 to a new closing high of 5,442 points on Monday.

Toronto's rise has been propelled by gold fever as stronger bullion prices prompted an upswing in the heavily weighted gold firms. Also, Canada's strengthening economy has sparked interest in the important natural resource stocks among international investors.
Analysts say natural resource firms can expect higher production and thus earnings during economic recovery.
"The markets have been doing well for such a lengthy period of time that investors are getting more confident all the time that it's going to last," Shay said.
"Companies are thinking it's a good time to go to the market, they're not concerned that they're not going to get in trouble from a falling market," Shay said.
"They're trying to take advantage of the fact that people are interested in buying equities right now," he added. "We're swamped."
Toronto, which is the world's 10th busiest stock exchange, has also seen a jump in initial public offerings.
"IPO activity is high, just like everything else," Shay said. So far this year, the TSE has seen 46 new issues, compared to 13 in the same period a year ago. In 1987, there were 113 IPOs.
Existing TSE-listed firms are also taking advantage of investor optimism. "Companies that are already around are raising a lot of money by issuing shares. That's very active as well," Shay said.
Share offerings from TSE-listed firms have doubled from a year earlier.

Across Canada, there were more than 160 equity issues exceeding C$10 million ($7.39 million) each by Sept. 30 for a total value of C$12 billion ($8.9 million), according to public information. That total is expected to top 200 issues by the end of October.
